title: Some Dolphins Wear Sponges on Their Noses. There's a Reason

scenes.text: Some dolphins wear a sponge on their nose. And they teach their kids to do it.
In Shark Bay, Australia, they tear basket sponges off the seafloor and carry them on their beaks.
Their prey hides in rough sand, and the sponge works like a protective glove.
Fish like the sandperch have no swim bladder, so they're hard to find with echolocation.
Calves spend years learning from their mothers, and the skill passes most often from mother to daughter.
A dolphin tool kit, handed down for generations.

description:
